values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline expansion supplies the Tennessee Valley Authority's new gas plant at the Kingston site in Tennessee. In February 2026 the authority said growing demand from data centers, population, and employment drove its decision to build the plant and keep the Kingston coal units running longer. The two sources are Enbridge's project page for the pipeline and a February 2026 news report on the authority's board vote.

verifications.note: Enbridge page says the project supplies gas for the Kingston plant replacement.
Television station report on the February 2026 board vote. The authority says demand growth driven by data centers, population, and employment created the need for the new gas plant at Kingston.

records.researcher_notes: The pipeline serves the new Tennessee Valley Authority gas plant at Kingston. The authority named data center growth among the reasons for that plant. No single data center campus is named, so this is an indirect tie. The earlier pass found nothing because it looked only at the pipeline pages.

values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline would carry gas to the planned 2,200 megawatt Dominion Energy and Santee Cooper gas plant on the former Canadys coal site in Colleton County, South Carolina. A May 2026 SC Daily Gazette report says utility executives call the plant essential for rapid population and industrial growth, and the reporter adds that this growth includes a ballooning number of energy-intensive data centers. The utilities' own approval statements found do not mention data centers. No single data center is named as a customer.

verifications.note: October 2025 news report says Santee Cooper and Dominion contracted Kinder Morgan to build the $431 million pipeline from Screven County, Georgia, to the Canadys plant site.

May 2026 news report says the plant is needed amid growth that includes a ballooning number of energy-intensive data centers, and that the Kinder Morgan pipeline will feed it. Read through a Wayback copy because the live site blocks plain fetches.

records.researcher_notes: The Kinder Morgan Bridge pipeline feeds the Canadys gas plant. Utility executives name data centers among the reasons for the plant. Both refs are from the same newspaper, so they are not independent. No named data center customer was found. Judgment call: the data center line in the Gazette is the reporter's summary, not a direct utility quote. A separate pass on South System Expansion 4 found that a data center developer said in September 2026 it is not tied to Canadys, and that otherwise only critics link Canadys to data centers.

ledger.note: Tagged yes through the Tennessee Valley Authority's Kingston gas plant, which the authority ties to data center demand growth.

Checked Enbridge's program pages and a search for data center ties. The program realigns the existing system and adds no new capacity for a named plant or customer. No data center tie or plant tie was found.
